--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.layout_bipartite()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Place the two sides of a bipartite graph in two parallel lines. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.layout_bipartite()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Place the two sides of a bipartite graph in two parallel lines. title: >- [Graph.layout_bipartite()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Place the two sides of a bipartite graph in two parallel lines. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Place the two sides of a bipartite graph in two parallel lines. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6002-L6169){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.layout_bipartite( nodes=None, align="vertical", aspect_ratio=4 / 3, scale=1.0, center=(0.0, 0.0), attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Bipartite layout](../assets/graphs/layout-bipartite.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="On the left, a bipartite graph of seven nodes scattered at random, nodes 1 to 3 in the accent color and nodes 4 to 7 in teal. On the right, layout_bipartite(nodes=[1, 2, 3]) puts nodes 1 to 3 in a left column and the other four in a right column, so every edge runs across between the columns." width="100%"} The nodes in `nodes=` (the first side) go evenly spaced, in ID order, on the left line and all other nodes on the right line, `aspect_ratio=` times the height away. The layout is then centered and scaled so the largest coordinate is `scale=`. With `align="horizontal"` the lines run across instead, the first side on the bottom. This follows NetworkX's `bipartite_layout()`. If `nodes=` is not given the graph is two-colored (direction ignored), with the lowest-ID node of each connected component on the first side; a graph that isn't bipartite then raises `ValueError`. Two-line drawings suit affiliation networks (people and the groups they belong to), user-item graphs and matchings. Positions are stored as `[x, y]` lists in the `attr_name=` node attribute; see `layout_circular()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[list]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node IDs or labels on the first side. If `None` (default), the sides are found by two-coloring the graph. [align]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["vertical"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : `"vertical"` (default) for two vertical lines side by side, or `"horizontal"` for two horizontal lines one above the other. [aspect_ratio]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [4 / 3]{.doc-parameter-default} : Distance between the lines relative to their length. Default is `4/3`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Largest coordinate after rescaling. Default is `1.0`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Center of the layout, as `(x, y)`. Default is the origin. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the positions in. If `None` (default), uses `"pos"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the positions on the nodes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, tuple[float, float]], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to `(x, y)` tuples. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `nodes=` is `None` and the graph is not bipartite, `align=` is unknown, `aspect_ratio=` is not positive, or `scale=` or `center=` is invalid. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~bipartite_sets`) : Split a bipartite graph into its two sides. [](`~layout_multipartite`) : Place nodes in parallel lines, one per layer. [](`~plot`) : Draw the graph using stored positions. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The two sides of a complete bipartite graph are found by two-coloring, and placed in two columns: ::: {#f5dd1f8a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_complete_bipartite_graph(2, 3) pos = graph.layout_bipartite(return_dict=True) {n: (round(x, 3), round(y, 3)) for n, (x, y) in pos.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: (-1.0, -0.625), 2: (-1.0, 0.625), 3: (0.667, -0.625), 4: (0.667, 0.0), 5: (0.667, 0.625)} ``` ::: ::: ### Women and events In the 1930s, Davis, Gardner and Gardner recorded which of 18 women in a Southern town attended which of 14 social events. Passing the women as `nodes=` puts them in the left column, in order, and the events, numbered by date, in the right: ::: {#ceaddd76 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} davis = ec.davis_southern_women() women = davis.get_node_df().filter(bipartite=0)["id"].to_list() davis.layout_bipartite(nodes=women, aspect_ratio=0.75).plot( layout="pos", color_by="bipartite", label_by="label", node_size=10, width=640, height=720, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The edges form a band. The first women in the list went mostly to the early events and the last ones mostly to the late events, so the women fall into two groups. The middle events drew from both: E8 was attended by 14 of the 18 women, highlighted here: ::: {#35042bad .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} at_e8 = davis.get_neighbors("E8") davis.plot( layout="pos", highlight=["E8"] + [davis.get_label_from_id(n) for n in at_e8], highlight_edges=[(davis.get_label_from_id(n), "E8") for n in at_e8], label_by="label", node_size=10, width=640, height=720, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
